memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “Be still, and know that I am God.” — Psalm 46:10

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
The meaning of hurry-burry is to keep running without stopping, or acting without thoughtful reflection. Today, this spirit of haste has slowly entered even our spiritual lives. The world moves fast, but it rarely takes time to listen to the voice of God.
Through the prophet Jeremiah, God speaks clearly:
“Stand at the crossroads and look; ask for the ancient paths, ask where the good way is, and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it.’”
( Jeremiah 6:16 )
Hurry dims our spiritual vision. It reduces our ability to wait upon the Lord, to recognize His gentle voice, and to discern His leading. It is not that God has stopped speaking; the truth is, we have not prepared our hearts to listen in stillness.
Today, many are busy doing ministry for God, yet they do not give time to sit in the presence of God. More time is spent planning than praying. Haste overtakes sensitivity. Though outwardly we may appear successful, if God’s presence is missing within, we stand before Him as poor—clothed in rags.
The sons of Eli acted selfishly in the holy priestly ministry. They served without reverence, fear, or devotion. Their haste and self-interest destroyed their ministry and brought pain and danger upon the generations of Eli. Through this, God teaches us a serious truth: spiritual haste always produces spiritual loss.
As we stand at the entrance of a new year, God is not asking us to run faster—He is calling us to wait quietly before Him.
One single word from God is enough to guide an entire year.
Please remember:
Hurry destroys divine fellowship.
Waiting in God’s presence gives birth to revelation.
Wait. Listen attentively. Remain before God.
Receive His promised word—and then continue your journey.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “The reason why we do not have revival is that we are content to live without it.” — Leonard Ravenhill

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, quiet my heart and steady my spirit.
Let one word from You guide my entire year.
Deliver me from unnecessary haste and teach me to walk patiently in Your perfect timing. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Do not rush into the new year.
Walk in the path led by His voice.
Waiting patiently in God’s presence will cause you to lose nothing in life’s journey.
Wait upon the Lord—and learn the higher things.

recommended_book.label: Recommended Book
recommended_book.title: Why Revival Tarries
recommended_book.author: Leonard Ravenhill
recommended_book.quote: Revival delays not because God is unwilling, but because people have become satisfied with haste and religious activity. Silence, prayer, repentance, and waiting in God’s presence are the strong roots of true revival. Speed silences the voice of God, and haste itself becomes a barrier to revival.
